title: Palo Alto Networks Certified Network Security Associate (PCNSA)

nodes.title: Security Profiles: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Security Profiles. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A security policy rule allows web-browsing traffic. The admin also attaches an A?
flashcards.back: Security policy rules determine allow or deny. Security profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, etc.) define what happens to traffic that the policy permits — they inspect it for threats and can reset, drop, or alert on individual threat events without necessarily blocking the entire session. The two constructs are complementary, not redundant. the attached profiles inspect the permitted traffic for threats without affecting the allow decision

flashcards.front: Which security profile is specifically designed to detect traffic from an alread?
flashcards.back: Anti-Spyware profiles target the outbound C2 communication stage of an attack — when an already-infected host attempts to beacon or receive commands from an external controller. Vulnerability Protection protects against inbound exploits. Antivirus scans file content. WildFire analyzes unknown files, not established C2 traffic patterns.

flashcards.front: A security admin creates multiple security rules that each require the same six ?
flashcards.back: A Security Profile Group bundles multiple individual profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, URL Filtering, File Blocking, WildFire) into a named group. Applying the group to a rule is a single selection, and updating the group propagates changes to all rules using it — greatly reducing effort compared to updating six individual profiles per rule.

flashcards.front: A network admin configures a Vulnerability Protection profile with action 'block?
flashcards.back: The 'block-ip' action in threat profiles dynamically adds the offending source IP to a block list for a configurable period (e.g., 300 seconds), preventing all subsequent connections from that IP during the block window. 'Drop' silently discards the offending packet/session. 'Reset-client' or 'reset-server' sends TCP RST. 'block-ip' is more aggressive, effectively quarantining the attacker. preventing all future traffic from that IP for a configured duration

pairs.stem: A security admin creates multiple security rules that each require the same six security profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, URL Filtering, File Blocking, WildFire). What Palo Alto construct reduces management overhead and ensures consistency?
pairs.option: A Security Profile Group that bundles all six profiles under a single name, which is applied to each rule

pairs.stem: A security policy rule allows web-browsing traffic. The admin also attaches an Antivirus profile and a Vulnerability Protection profile to the same rule. Which statement best describes this configuration?
pairs.option: The security policy controls whether traffic is permitted;.

pairs.stem: What is the function of the 'Antivirus' security profile compared to the 'WildFire Analysis' profile in threat prevention?
pairs.option: Antivirus handles executable files while WildFire handles only document formats (PDF, Office) — they cover different file types

pairs.stem: A threat log shows a high-severity exploit attempt was detected by the Vulnerability Protection profile and the action taken was 'alert'. The admin wants to change this to automatically block such attacks. What should be modified?
pairs.option: The threat exception list in the Anti-Spyware profile, overriding the default action to block for that signature ID

pairs.stem: Which security profile is specifically designed to detect traffic from an already-infected internal host attempting to reach a command-and-control server on the internet?
pairs.option: WildFire, which sandboxes outbound executables before they can be transmitted to external servers

pairs.stem: A security engineer configures a File Blocking profile to block users from uploading .exe files to any cloud storage application. In which section of the security policy rule is this profile applied?
pairs.option: Under the Profile Settings section of the security rule, in the same area as AV and IPS profiles

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A firewall forwards an unknown executable file to WildFire for analysis. The fil?
flashcards.back: After determining a malware verdict, WildFire automatically generates threat/antivirus signatures and distributes them globally to all subscribed firewalls, typically within five minutes. This protects the entire subscriber base from the same threat quickly. WildFire does not retroactively terminate established sessions or require manual approval for signature creation. typically within minutes

flashcards.front: A WildFire verdict returns 'grayware' for a file sent from an internal host. Wha?
flashcards.back: WildFire uses four verdicts: benign (clean), malware (confirmed malicious — signature generated), grayware (potentially unwanted programs like adware, spyware lite, or surveillance tools — lower severity), and phishing (credential theft pages). Grayware is not definitively malicious malware but may warrant attention based on policy. Organizations can configure WildFire profiles to block or alert on grayware. surveillance tools) but is not classified as malware

flashcards.front: An organization operates in a classified environment with no internet access. Th?
flashcards.back: The WF-500 WildFire appliance is a private cloud sandbox device that can be deployed on-premises for air-gapped or highly regulated environments. It performs the same multi-OS sandbox analysis as the public WildFire cloud but without sending files externally. WildFire Inline ML performs local ML-based analysis but is not a full sandbox and handles fewer file types.

flashcards.front: An enterprise manages 50 Palo Alto firewalls across 10 branch offices. Which Pal?
flashcards.back: Panorama is Palo Alto's centralized management platform. Device groups push security policies to sets of firewalls; templates push device configuration (interfaces, zones, routing). Panorama also centralizes logging. AutoFocus is a threat intelligence product, Cortex XSOAR is a SOAR platform, and Expedition is a migration utility.

pairs.stem: A security architect wants to assess network traffic and understand application usage before deploying a new firewall inline. Which deployment mode provides visibility without any risk of disrupting production traffic?
pairs.option: Tap mode, where the firewall receives a copy of traffic via a SPAN port and analyzes it without being inline

pairs.stem: A Palo Alto firewall address object named 'mail-server' is defined as FQDN 'mail.company.com'. What is the benefit of using an FQDN address object compared to a static IP address object in security policy?
pairs.option: FQDN objects are resolved at commit time and embedded as IP addresses, so they perform faster than static IP lookups

pairs.stem: A security team wants firewall policies to reflect user identities from Active Directory rather than IP addresses. Which Palo Alto feature maps Windows AD logon events to IP addresses for use in security policy?
pairs.option: Captive portal only, which requires every user to authenticate through a browser redirect

pairs.stem: An enterprise manages 50 Palo Alto firewalls across 10 branch offices. Which Palo Alto product provides centralized policy management, configuration deployment via device groups, and log aggregation?
pairs.option: Panorama, which uses device groups for policy management and templates for device configuration across all managed firewalls

pairs.stem: A firewall forwards an unknown executable file to WildFire for analysis. The file is later confirmed as malware. What actions does WildFire take after determining the verdict?
pairs.option: WildFire generates a new antivirus/threat signature and distributes it to all subscribers,.

pairs.stem: A network admin wants to block peer-to-peer applications like BitTorrent regardless of which port they use. Which Palo Alto technology makes this possible without manually tracking every port used?
pairs.option: A URL filtering profile configured to block the BitTorrent website category
